recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Revisit only if a future work-group decision asks for a new module-taxonomy explanation; FHIR-7471 does not require a current core source edit.
issue_request: FHIR-7471 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification DSTU1 FHIR-core clarification request. It reported that ProcedureRequest and VisionPrescription appeared under Administrative while MedicationPrescription and DiagnosticOrder appeared under Clinical, making the classification criteria unclear; the accepted resolution was to clarify resourceguide.html.
initial_application: No git commit explicitly mentioning FHIR-7471 or old core #766 was found. The apparent application path is the August 2015 resource-guide work: commit 014e9d175437d999b5090e29b7488198cb5e9263 introduced Clinical resource classification content including the named resources, and commits 7524d34dddf437435b8624f9ebf4a180ec80e42f and bb5e3f2a9fcb50aecda21994cda00fdc6981b0c8 overhauled and drafted the resource guide after Jira comments said the work was ongoing.
additional_context: The current build-scope source uses resourceguide.html and clinicalsummary-module.html from source/hierarchy.xml. The original resource names have been renamed or merged: DiagnosticOrder and ProcedureRequest are now ServiceRequest, MedicationPrescription is now MedicationRequest, and VisionPrescription remains active. Current publish.ini and StructureDefinition metadata classify MedicationRequest, ServiceRequest, and VisionPrescription under Clinical categories. The Administration module describes base data linked into clinical content, while the Clinical module covers core clinical information and delegates diagnostics/medications to their modules. Later FHIR-13042 removed most rendered resource-guide classification tables, so editing the commented historical block would not improve the current build.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current specification no longer presents the original Administrative-versus-Clinical inconsistency, and existing module/category/resource-guide sources provide sufficient current classification context.
